#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const int MAXN = 85;

int n, m;
int grid[MAXN][MAXN];
vector<pair<int, int>> pos[20005]; // positions for each pair number

int main() {
    cin >> n >> m;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < m; j++) {
            cin >> grid[i][j];
            pos[grid[i][j]].push_back({i, j});
        }
    }

    int total = n * m;
    int max_pairs = total / 2;
    vector<vector<int>> dp(max_pairs + 1, vector<int>(max_pairs + 1, 0));

    // Initialize DP
    for (int i = 0; i <= max_pairs; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j <= max_pairs; j++) {
            dp[i][j] = 0;
        }
    }

    // Fill DP table
    for (int i = 1; i <= max_pairs; i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= max_pairs; j++) {
            // Option 1: don't pair i-th and j-th pairs
            dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]);

            // Option 2: pair i-th and j-th pairs
            int pair_i = i - 1;
            int pair_j = j - 1;

            // Get positions for pair_i and pair_j
            auto& p1 = pos[pair_i + 1]; // since pair numbers start from 1
            auto& p2 = pos[pair_j + 1];

            // Calculate Manhattan distance between the two pairs
            int dist = abs(p1[0].first - p2[0].first) + abs(p1[0].second - p2[0].second) +
                       abs(p1[1].first - p2[1].first) + abs(p1[1].second - p2[1].second);

            // Update DP table
            dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j], dp[i-1][j-1] + dist);
        }
    }

    // The answer is the maximum distance we can achieve by pairing all pairs
    cout << dp[max_pairs][max_pairs] << endl;

    return 0;
}
